title.raw: 卷二十八 列傳第十八 褚裕之 Volume 28 Biographies 18: Chu Yuzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第十八

translations.literal: Biographies 18
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 18

sentences.zh: 褚裕之

translations.literal: Chu Yuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuzhi

sentences.zh: 秀之弟淡之字仲原，亦曆顯官，為宋武帝車騎從事中郎，尚書吏部郎，廷尉卿，左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Danzhi, styled Zhongyuan, also rose through prominent offices, serving as Attendant-in-Ordinary to Emperor Wu of Song's Chariots and Cavalry, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of Justice, and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Danzhi, styled Zhongyuan, likewise climbed through high office: Attendant-in-Ordinary on Liu Yu's Chariots and Cavalry staff, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of Justice, and General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 宋受命，為侍中。

translations.literal: When Song received the mandate, he became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Song took the throne, he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 淡之兄弟並盡忠事武帝，恭帝每生男，輒令方便殺焉，或誘賂內人，或密加毒害，前後如此非一。

translations.literal: The Danzhi brothers both served Emperor Wu with full loyalty; whenever Emperor Gong bore a son, they were ordered to find a convenient way to kill him—sometimes by bribing palace women, sometimes by secret poison—and this happened more than once.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhi and his brothers served Liu Yu with utter loyalty. Each time Emperor Gong fathered a son, they were told to kill the child by whatever means they could—bribing inner attendants, slipping in poison—and this happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 及恭帝遜位居秣陵宮，常懼見禍，與褚後共止一室，慮有酖毒，自煮食於前。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong abdicated and lived at Moling Palace, he constantly feared disaster; he and Empress Chu shared one room, dreading poisoned food, and cooked for himself in their presence.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong yielded the throne and moved to Moling Palace, he lived in constant fear. He and Empress Chu stayed in one room, suspecting poison in every dish, and he cooked his own meals before them.

sentences.zh: 武帝將殺之，不欲遣人入內，令淡之兄弟視後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was about to kill him but did not wish to send men inside; he had the Danzhi brothers keep watch on the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu decided to kill Gong, he did not want soldiers entering the palace and ordered the Danzhi brothers to keep Empress Chu occupied.

sentences.zh: 褚後出別室相見，兵人乃踰垣而入，進藥於恭帝。

translations.literal: When Empress Chu went to another room to meet him, soldiers scaled the wall, entered, and presented the drug to Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Chu was summoned to a separate room, soldiers climbed the wall, entered, and brought poison to Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 帝不肯飲，曰：「佛教自殺者不得復人身。

translations.literal: The emperor refused to drink and said, "In Buddhism, one who commits suicide cannot be reborn in human form.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused the cup. "Buddhist law holds that suicide bars rebirth as a human being,

sentences.zh: 」乃以被掩殺之。

translations.literal: " So they smothered him with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: " So they smothered him beneath a quilt.

sentences.zh: 後會稽郡缺，朝議欲用蔡廓，武帝曰：「彼自是蔡家佳兒，何關人事。

translations.literal: Later the post of Grand Administrator of Kuaiji fell vacant; court discussion favored Cai Kuo, but Emperor Wu said, "He is simply a fine son of the Cai family—what has that to do with the appointment?
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaiji needed a new grand administrator, the court favored Cai Kuo. Liu Yu said, "He is a good scion of the Cai house—what does that have to do with filling the post?

sentences.zh: 可用褚佛。

translations.literal: Chu Fo may be used.
translations.idiomatic: Use Chu Fo instead.

sentences.zh: 」佛，淡之小字也。

translations.literal: " Fo was Danzhi's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Fo was Danzhi's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 乃用淡之為會稽太守。

translations.literal: Danzhi was then appointed Grand Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhi was appointed Grand Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 景平元年，富陽孫氏聚合門宗謀逆，其支黨在永興縣潛相影響。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping, the Sun clan of Fuyang gathered their kinsmen to plot rebellion; their partisans in Yongxing County secretly coordinated with them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingping 1 the Sun clan of Fuyang rallied their lineage to rebel, while allies in Yongxing County worked in secret concert.

sentences.zh: 永興令羊恂覺其謀，以告淡之，淡之不信，乃以誣人之罪收縣職局。

translations.literal: Yongxing Magistrate Yang Xun detected the plot and reported it to Danzhi; Danzhi did not believe him and instead arrested the county staff on a charge of false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing Magistrate Yang Xun uncovered the plot and warned Danzhi, who disbelieved him and jailed the county clerks for slander.

sentences.zh: 於是孫法先自號冠軍大將軍，與孫道慶等攻沒縣邑，更相樹置，遙以鄮令司馬文宣為征西大將軍，建旗鳴鼓，直攻山陰。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sun Faxian styled himself Grand General Champion and, with Sun Daoqing and others, seized the county seat; they set up rival offices and, from afar, named Kuaiji Magistrate Sima Wenxuan Grand General Who Conquers the West; raising banners and beating drums, they marched straight on Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Faxian then proclaimed himself Grand General Champion. With Sun Daoqing and others he overran the county town, installed rival offices, and named Kuaiji Magistrate Sima Wenxuan Grand General Who Conquers the West; banners aloft and drums sounding, they drove on Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 淡之自假陵江將軍，以山陰令陸邵領司馬，加振武將軍，前員外散騎常侍王茂之為長史，前國子博士孔欣、前員外散騎常侍謝苓之並參軍事，召行參軍七十餘人。

translations.literal: Danzhi personally assumed the title General Who Crosses the River, made Shanyin Magistrate Lu Shao his chief aide with the added rank General Who Quells Martial Foes, appointed former Supernumerary Regular Palace Attendant Wang Maozhi as chief secretary, former Doctor of the National University Kong Xin and former Supernumerary Regular Palace Attendant Xie Lingzhi as staff officers, and summoned more than seventy acting staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhi took the provisional title General Who Crosses the River, made Shanyin Magistrate Lu Shao his chief aide with the added rank General Who Quells Martial Foes, named former Supernumerary Regular Palace Attendant Wang Maozhi chief secretary, and put former National University Doctor Kong Xin and former Supernumerary Regular Palace Attendant Xie Lingzhi on his staff, calling up more than seventy acting staff officers.

sentences.zh: 前鎮西諮議參軍孔甯子、左光祿大夫孔季恭子山士並在艱中，皆起為將軍。

translations.literal: Former Staff Officer to the General Who Guards the West Kong Ningzi and Kong Jigong's son Shanshi, son of Left Grand Master of the Palace Kong Jigong, were both in mourning yet were summoned and made generals.
translations.idiomatic: Former Staff Officer Kong Ningzi and Kong Jigong's son Shanshi were both in mourning when Danzhi pulled them from bereavement and made them generals.

sentences.zh: 遣隊主陳願、郡議曹掾虞道納二軍過浦陽江。

translations.literal: He sent squad leaders Chen Yuan and county staff officer Yu Daona with two armies across the Puyang River.
translations.idiomatic: He sent squad leaders Chen Yuan and county staff officer Yu Daona with two detachments across the Puyang River.

sentences.zh: 願等戰敗，賊遂推鋒而前，去城二十餘里。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others were defeated, and the rebels pressed forward to within twenty-odd li of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan's force was beaten, and the rebels drove to within twenty-odd li of the city.

sentences.zh: 淡之遣陸邵水軍禦之，而身率所領出次近郊。

translations.literal: Danzhi sent Lu Shao with the river fleet to resist them while he personally led his troops to encamp near the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhi sent Lu Shao's river force to meet them and personally led his own troops to camp just outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 邵與行參軍漏恭期合力，大敗賊于柯亭。

translations.literal: Lu Shao and acting staff officer Lou Gongqi joined forces and routed the rebels at Keting.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shao and acting staff officer Lou Gongqi combined their forces and crushed the rebels at Keting.

sentences.zh: 淡之尋卒，諡曰質子。

translations.literal: Danzhi soon died; his posthumous title was Zhi Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhi died soon after; his posthumous name was Zhi Zi.

sentences.zh: 裕之名與武帝同，故行字焉。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's given name matched the emperor's, so he used his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuzhi shared the emperor's given name, he went by his style name instead.

sentences.zh: 初為太宰琅邪王行參軍，武帝車騎參軍，司徒左西屬，中軍諮議參軍，署中兵，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was acting staff officer to the Prince of Langye, Grand Preceptor; staff officer on Emperor Wu's Chariots and Cavalry staff; Left Western Aide under the Minister of Education; Staff Officer to the General Who Guards the Army; acting commander of central troops; and was given the rank General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He began as acting staff officer to the Prince of Langye, Grand Preceptor; served on Liu Yu's Chariots and Cavalry staff; became Left Western Aide under the Minister of Education; then Staff Officer to the General Who Guards the Army, acting commander of central troops, with the added rank General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 從征鮮卑，盡其誠力。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Xianbei and gave his utmost loyalty and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the Xianbei and gave everything he had to the campaign.

sentences.zh: 盧循攻查浦，叔度力戰有功。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun attacked Zhapu, Shudu fought hard and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun struck Zhapu, Shudu fought fiercely and earned distinction.

sentences.zh: 循南走，武帝板行廣州刺史，加督，建威將軍，領平越中郎將。

translations.literal: When Xun fled south, Emperor Wu appointed him acting Governor of Guangzhou with supervisory authority, General Who Establishes Might, and Colonel Director of the Pacification of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun fled south, Liu Yu appointed him acting Governor of Guangzhou with supervisory authority, General Who Establishes Might, and Colonel Director of the Pacification of Yue.

sentences.zh: 在任四年，廣營貲貨，資財豐積，坐免官，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: During four years in office he amassed goods on a wide scale and piled up wealth; for this he was dismissed, stripped of office, and confined for life.
translations.idiomatic: In four years as governor he traded on a vast scale and hoarded wealth; he was dismissed, stripped of rank, and confined for life.

sentences.zh: 還至都，凡諸親舊及一面之款，無不厚加贈遺。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, he lavishly bestowed gifts on every relative, old friend, and even casual acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, he showered gifts on relatives, old friends, and even people he had met only once.

sentences.zh: 尋除太尉諮議參軍、相國右司馬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and Right Marshal of the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and Right Marshal under the Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate, he became General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu took the throne, he became General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其名家，而能竭盡心力，甚嘉之，封番禺縣男。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because he came from an eminent house yet exerted himself to the full, greatly praised him and enfeoffed him as Baron of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu admired that a man of such a great clan had served so wholeheartedly and enfeoffed him as Baron of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was soon given the added rank Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the added rank Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，出為雍州刺史，領甯蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he went out as Inspector of Yong Province and Colonel Director of the Pacification of the Man.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 3 he was sent out as Inspector of Yong Province and Colonel Director of the Pacification of the Man.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，以清簡致稱。

translations.literal: During three years in office he won repute for purity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: In three years as inspector he earned a name for clean and spare government.

sentences.zh: 景平二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingping 2.

sentences.zh: 子恬之嗣。

translations.literal: His son Tianzhi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianzhi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 恬之弟寂之，著作佐郎，早卒。

translations.literal: Tianzhi's younger brother Jizhi was Assistant Director in the Office of Compilation and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhi's younger brother Jizhi served as Assistant Director in the Office of Compilation and died young.

sentences.zh: 寂之子曖尚宋文帝第六女琅邪貞長公主，位太宰參軍，亦早卒。

translations.literal: Jizhi's son Ai married the sixth daughter of Emperor Wen of Song, Princess Zhen of Langye, held the post of Staff Officer to the Grand Preceptor, and also died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's son Ai married Emperor Wen's sixth daughter, Princess Zhen of Langye, served as Staff Officer to the Grand Preceptor, and likewise died young.

sentences.zh: 曖子繢位太子舍人，亦尚宋公主。

translations.literal: Ai's son Hui held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent and also married a princess of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Ai's son Hui was Attendant of the Heir Apparent and also married a Song princess.

sentences.zh: 繢子球字仲寶，少孤貧，篤志好學，有才思。

translations.literal: Hui's son Qiu, styled Zhongbao, was orphaned and poor in youth, yet devoted himself to study with firm resolve and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Qiu, styled Zhongbao, lost his parents young and grew up in poverty, yet studied with single-minded devotion and showed real literary gift.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素，元徽中誅滅，唯有一女存，故吏何昌寓、王思遠聞球清立，以此女妻之。

translations.literal: When Prince Jing of Pingping of Song was executed in the Yuanhui era, only one daughter survived; former retainers He Changyu and Wang Siyuan, hearing of Qiu's upright character, gave her to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jing of Pingping was destroyed in the Yuanhui era, only one daughter remained. Former retainers He Changyu and Wang Siyuan, hearing of Qiu's upright character, married her to him.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為溧陽令，在縣清白，資公奉而已。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he was magistrate of Liyang; in the county he remained clean and lived only on his official salary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as magistrate of Liyang, governing cleanly and living on his salary alone.

sentences.zh: 仕梁曆都官尚書，通直散騎常侍，秘書監，領著作，司徒右長史，常侍、著作如故。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he rose through the posts of Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Director of Compilation, Right Chief Secretary to the Minister of Education, and retained his posts as Regular Attendant and Director of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he rose to Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Director of the Secretariat with concurrent charge of Compilation, and Right Chief Secretary to the Minister of Education, keeping his posts as Regular Attendant and Director of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 自魏孫禮、晉荀組以後，台佐加貂，始自球也。

translations.literal: Since Wei's Sun Li and Jin's Xun Zu, no secretariat aide had worn the marten tail until Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sun Li of Wei and Xun Zu of Jin, no secretariat aide had worn the marten insignia until Qiu.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎常侍，光祿大夫，加給事中。

translations.literal: Later he became Regular Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and was given the added post Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Regular Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the added post Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑逆，以為吏部尚書，復出為丹陽尹，統石頭戍事。

translations.literal: When the crown prince committed regicide, Qiu was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then sent out again as Intendant of Danyang and put in charge of the garrison at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince murdered his father, Qiu was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then sent out again as Intendant of Danyang with command of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 孝武入伐，劭自攻新亭壘，使湛之率水師俱進，湛之因攜二息彥回、澄，登輕舟南奔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched in to attack, Shao himself assaulted the fortress at Xinting and ordered Yuanzhi to lead the river force forward together; Yuanzhi thereupon took his two sons Yanhui and Cheng, boarded a light boat, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu marched to attack him, Shao personally assaulted the Xinting fortress and ordered Yuanzhi to advance with the river fleet; Yuanzhi instead took his sons Yanhui and Cheng aboard a light boat and fled south.

sentences.zh: 彥回始生一男，為劭所殺。

translations.literal: Yanhui had just borne a son, who was killed by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui had just had a son, whom Shao had killed.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，以為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Yuanzhi was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu ascended the throne, Yuanzhi was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，為中書令、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian he became Director of the Secretariat and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1 he became Director of the Secretariat and Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 後拜尚書左僕射，以南奔賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and, for fleeing south, was granted the title Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and, for his flight south, enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 大明四年卒，諡敬侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daming 4; his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子彥回。

translations.literal: His son was Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 彥回幼有清譽。

translations.literal: Yanhui had a reputation for purity from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui enjoyed a reputation for purity from childhood.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，魏軍逼瓜步，百姓咸負擔而立。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era of Song, Wei troops pressed Guabu and the common people all stood bearing loads on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song's Yuanjia era, when Wei armies pressed Guabu, common people stood everywhere with packs on their backs.

sentences.zh: 時父湛之為丹陽尹，使其子弟並著芒屩，于齋前習行。

translations.literal: At the time his father Yuanzhi was Intendant of Danyang and had his sons and younger relatives all wear straw sandals and drill marching in the courtyard before the fast hall.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhi, then Intendant of Danyang, made his sons and younger kinsmen wear straw sandals and practice marching in the courtyard before the fast hall.

sentences.zh: 或譏之，湛之曰：「安不忘危也。

translations.literal: Some mocked this; Yuanzhi said, "In peace one must not forget danger.
translations.idiomatic: When others mocked this, Yuanzhi said, "In peace one must not forget danger.

sentences.zh: 」彥回時年十餘，甚有慚色。

translations.literal: " Yanhui was then in his teens and felt deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui, then in his teens, flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 湛之有一牛，至所愛，無故墮聽事前井，湛之率左右躬自營救之，郡中喧擾，彥回下簾不視也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi had an ox he loved dearly; it fell for no reason into the well before the audience hall. Yuanzhi led his attendants to rescue it personally, throwing the prefecture into uproar; Yanhui lowered the curtain and would not look.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi owned a beloved ox that suddenly fell into the well before the audience hall. He led his attendants to haul it out himself, throwing the prefecture into uproar; Yanhui lowered his curtain and refused to watch.

sentences.zh: 又有門生盜其衣，彥回遇見，謂曰：「可密藏之，勿使人見。

translations.literal: There was also a student who stole his clothes; Yanhui encountered him and said, "Hide them carefully—do not let anyone see.
translations.idiomatic: Once a student stole his clothes; Yanhui caught him and said, "Hide them well—do not let anyone see.

sentences.zh: 」此門生慚而去，不敢復還，後貴乃歸罪，待之如初。

translations.literal: " The student left in shame and did not dare return; only after he had risen in rank did he come back to confess guilt, and Yanhui treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: " The student fled in shame and did not return until he had risen in rank, when he came to confess; Yanhui treated him exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 尚宋文帝女南郡獻公主，拜駙馬都尉，除著作佐郎，累遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Emperor Wen of Song, Princess Xian of Nankang, was appointed Commandant Escort, made Assistant Director in the Office of Compilation, and rose to Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Wen's daughter, Princess Xian of Nankang, became Commandant Escort, served as Assistant Director in the Office of Compilation, and rose to Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湛之卒，彥回悉推財與弟澄，唯取書數千卷。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhi died, Yanhui turned over all the property to his younger brother Cheng and kept only several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhi died, Yanhui gave all the family wealth to his brother Cheng and kept only a few thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 湛之有兩廚寶物，在彥回所生郭氏間，嫡母吳郡主求之，郭欲不與，彥回曰：「但令彥回在，何患無物。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi had two storerooms of valuables kept with Yanhui's birth mother, the Guo family; his stepmother, the Lady of Wu Commandery, demanded them, and Guo wished to refuse; Yanhui said, "So long as Yanhui lives, why worry about lacking things?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi had two storerooms of valuables held by Yanhui's birth mother, Lady Guo; his stepmother, the Lady of Wu Commandery, demanded them, and Guo wished to refuse. Yanhui said, "While I live, why fear we shall lack for anything?

sentences.zh: 」猶不許，彥回流涕固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: " She still would not agree; Yanhui wept and pleaded until she yielded.
translations.idiomatic: " She still refused; Yanhui wept and pleaded until she yielded.

sentences.zh: 襲爵都鄉侯，歷位尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Marquis of Duxiang and rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Duxiang and rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 景和中，山陰公主淫恣，窺見彥回悅之，以白帝。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era, Princess Shanyin was licentious and unrestrained; seeing Yanhui, she took a liking to him and reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era, Princess Shanyin was wanton and unrestrained; seeing Yanhui, she desired him and told the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝召彥回西上合宿十日，公主夜就之，備見逼迫，彥回整身而立，從夕至曉，不為移志。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yanhui to lodge ten days in the upper western pavilion; the princess came to him by night with every form of pressure, but Yanhui stood upright from evening till dawn and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yanhui to lodge ten days in the upper western pavilion. The princess came by night and pressed him in every way, but Yanhui stood straight from dusk till dawn and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 公主謂曰：「君須髯如戟，何無丈夫意？

translations.literal: The princess said to him, "Your beard and brows are like halberds—why show no manly spirit?
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "With beard and brows like halberds, why show no manly spirit?

sentences.zh: 「彥回曰：「回雖不敏，何敢首為亂階。」

translations.literal: " Yanhui said, "Though Hui is no clever man, how would I dare be the first to start disorder?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui replied, "Though I am no clever man, how would I dare be the first to start disorder?"

sentences.zh: 帝之在蕃，與彥回以風素相善，至是深相委仗，陳事皆見從。

translations.literal: When the emperor was still a prince, he and Yanhui were close in character and disposition; now he relied on him deeply, and whatever Yanhui proposed was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had still been a prince, he and Yanhui had been close in character; now he relied on him deeply, and Yanhui's proposals were always accepted.

sentences.zh: 改封雩都伯，曆侍中，領尚書，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Baron of Yudu; he served as Palace Attendant, concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Baron of Yudu; he served as Palace Attendant, concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 彥回美儀貌，善容止，俯仰進退，咸有風則。

translations.literal: Yanhui had handsome features and graceful bearing; in every movement, bow, advance, or retreat, he showed true dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was handsome and graceful; in every bow, step, advance, or retreat he showed true dignity.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，百僚遠國使，莫不延首目送之。

translations.literal: At every court assembly, officials and envoys from distant states all craned their necks and watched him depart.
translations.idiomatic: At every court assembly, officials and envoys from distant lands craned their necks to watch him pass.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘗歎曰：「褚彥回能遲行緩步，便得宰相矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming once sighed and said, "If Chu Yanhui can walk slowly and with measured step, he will become a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming once sighed, "Chu Yanhui need only walk slowly and with measured step to become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」時人以方何平叔。

translations.literal: " People of the time compared him to He Pingshu.
translations.idiomatic: " People of the time compared him to He Pingshu.

sentences.zh: 嘗聚袁粲舍，初秋涼夕，風月甚美，彥回援琴奏別鵠之曲，宮商既調，風神諧暢。

translations.literal: Once gathered at Yuan Can's house on a cool early-autumn evening with a beautiful moon and breeze, Yanhui took up the zither and played the melody "Parting Geese"; once the tones were tuned, his spirit flowed in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at Yuan Can's house on a cool early-autumn evening under a fine moon and breeze, Yanhui took up the zither and played "Parting Geese"; once the tones were tuned, his spirit flowed in harmony.

sentences.zh: 王彧、謝莊並在粲坐，撫節而歎曰：「以無累之神，合有道之器，宮商暫離，不可得已。」

translations.literal: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were both at Yuan's gathering; beating time, they sighed and said, "With a spirit free of burden joined to an instrument of the Way, even a brief parting of tones cannot be endured."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were present; beating time, they sighed, "A spirit free of burden joined to an instrument of the Way—when the tones part even briefly, one cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 時傖人常珍奇與薛安都為逆，降叛非一。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian Chang Zhenqi joined Xue Andu in rebellion, surrendering and revolting more than once.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the barbarian Chang Zhenqi rebelled alongside Xue Andu, surrendering and revolting again and again.

sentences.zh: 後又求降，明帝加以重位。

translations.literal: Later he sought surrender again, and Emperor Ming gave him a high post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sought surrender again, and Emperor Ming gave him a high post.

sentences.zh: 彥回謂全其首領，于事已弘，不足大加寵異。

translations.literal: Yanhui said that sparing his life was already generous enough for the affair and that he did not deserve extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui argued that sparing his life was already generous and that he deserved no extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 珍奇尋又叛。

translations.literal: Zhenqi soon rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqi soon rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 彥回後為吳興太守，帝寢疾危殆，馳使召之，欲托後事。

translations.literal: Later Yanhui became Grand Administrator of Wuxing; the emperor fell gravely ill and sent a fast messenger to summon him, intending to entrust him with affairs after death.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui later became Grand Administrator of Wuxing. When the emperor fell gravely ill, he sent a fast messenger to summon him, intending to entrust him with the succession.

sentences.zh: 及至召入，帝坐帳中流涕曰：「吾近危篤，故召卿，欲使著黃羅裸。

translations.literal: When Yanhui arrived and was summoned in, the emperor sat within the curtain weeping and said, "I have lately been in mortal danger, so I summoned you—I wish you to wear the yellow gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhui arrived and was summoned in, the emperor sat within the curtain weeping. "I have been near death," he said, "so I summoned you—I wish you to wear the yellow gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 」指床頭大函曰：「文書皆函內置，此函不得復開。

translations.literal: " Pointing to a large case at the head of the bed, he said, "All documents are inside this case; this case must not be opened again.
translations.idiomatic: " He pointed to a large case at the head of the bed. "All documents are inside; this case must never be opened again.

sentences.zh: 」彥回亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: " Yanhui too was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui too was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 黃羅裸，乳母服也。

translations.literal: The yellow gauze robe was wet-nurse garb.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow gauze robe was wet-nurse garb.

sentences.zh: 帝雖小間，猶懷身後慮。

translations.literal: Though the emperor recovered somewhat, he still brooded over affairs after death.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor recovered somewhat, he still brooded over what would follow his death.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁，人才令美，物情宗向，帝與彥回謀誅之，彥回以為不可。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren was talented, handsome, and the object of public esteem; the emperor plotted with Yanhui to kill him, but Yanhui thought it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren was talented, handsome, and widely admired; the emperor plotted with Yanhui to kill him, but Yanhui thought it wrong.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「卿癡不足與議事。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said, "You are too stupid to discuss affairs with.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "You are too stupid to discuss affairs with.

sentences.zh: 」彥回懼而奉旨。

translations.literal: " Yanhui, in fear, obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui, afraid, obeyed.

sentences.zh: 復為吏部尚書，衛尉卿，尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of the Guard, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of the Guard, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以母老疾，晨昏須養，辭衛尉，不許。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old and ill and needed care morning and evening, he resigned the Guard ministry; the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old and ill and needed care morning and evening, he asked to resign the Guard ministry; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遺詔以為中書令、護軍將軍，與尚書令袁粲受顧命，輔幼主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, his final edict made Yanhui Director of the Secretariat and General Who Protects the Army; he and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Can received the dying charge to assist the young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, his final edict made Yanhui Director of the Secretariat and General Who Protects the Army; he and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Can received the dying charge to assist the young emperor.

sentences.zh: 粲等雖同見托，而意在彥回。

translations.literal: Though Can and the others were entrusted together, their hearts were set on Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Though Can and the others were entrusted together, their hearts were set on Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 彥回同心理事，務弘儉約，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Yanhui managed affairs with like mind, striving to promote thrift, and the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui managed affairs in concert with them, striving to promote thrift, and the people relied on him.

sentences.zh: 既而王道隆、阮佃夫用事，奸賂公行，彥回不能禁也。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Daolong and Ruan Tianfu held power; bribery and corruption ran openly, and Yanhui could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Daolong and Ruan Tianfu held power; bribery ran openly through the court, and Yanhui could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 遭所生喪，毀頓不復可識，期年不盥櫛，唯泣淚處乃見其本質焉。

translations.literal: When he suffered mourning for his birth mother, he was so wasted as to be unrecognizable; for a full year he did not wash or comb his hair, and only where tears fell could one see his true complexion.
translations.idiomatic: When his birth mother died, grief wasted him beyond recognition; for a full year he neither washed nor combed his hair, and only where tears had fallen could one see his true face.

sentences.zh: 詔斷哭，禁吊客。

translations.literal: An edict forbade weeping and barred mourners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade public weeping and barred mourners from calling.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，起為中軍將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: After the burial he was recalled as General of the Central Army, retaining his former posts.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he was recalled as General of the Central Army, keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，桂陽王休範反，彥回與衛將軍袁粲入衛宮省，鎮集眾心。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, Prince Guiyang Xiu Fan rebelled; Yanhui and General Who Guards the Army Yuan Can entered the palace to defend it and steady the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 2 Prince Guiyang Xiu Fan rebelled; Yanhui and General Who Guards the Army Yuan Can entered the palace to defend it and steady public morale.

sentences.zh: 彥回初為丹陽，與從弟照同載，道逢齊高帝，彥回舉手指高帝車謂照曰：「此非常人也。

translations.literal: When Yanhui was first Intendant of Danyang, he rode in the same carriage with his younger cousin Zhao; on the road they met the future Emperor Gao of Qi, and Yanhui pointed at Gao's carriage and said to Zhao, "This is no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhui was first Intendant of Danyang, he rode with his younger cousin Zhao and met the future Emperor Gao of Qi on the road. Yanhui pointed at Gao's carriage and said to Zhao, "That is no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 」出為吳興，高帝餉物別，彥回又語人曰：「此人才貌非常，將來不可測也。

translations.literal: " After he went out to Wuxing, Gao sent him gifts on parting, and Yanhui again told others, "This man's talent and appearance are extraordinary; the future cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: " After he left for Wuxing, Gao sent parting gifts, and Yanhui again told others, "That man's talent and bearing are extraordinary; his future cannot be measured.

sentences.zh: 」及顧命之際，引高帝豫焉。

translations.literal: " At the time of the dying charge, Gao was included in advance.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time of the dying charge, Gao was included among the regents.

sentences.zh: 高帝既平桂陽，遷中領軍，領南兗州，高帝固讓，與彥回及衛軍袁粲書陳情，彥回、粲答書不從，高帝乃受命。

translations.literal: After Gao had pacified Guiyang, he was transferred to Central Camp Commander with charge of South Yan Province; Gao firmly declined, writing to Yanhui and General Who Guards the Army Yuan Can to state his feelings; Yanhui and Can replied refusing to accept his refusal, and Gao then took the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao pacified Guiyang he was made Central Camp Commander with charge of South Yan Province. Gao firmly declined, writing to Yanhui and Yuan Can to explain himself; they answered refusing his refusal, and Gao then accepted.

sentences.zh: 其年加彥回尚書令、侍中，給班劍二十人，固讓令。

translations.literal: That year Yanhui was given the added posts Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant, with twenty guards bearing ceremonial swords; he firmly declined the directorship.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yanhui received the added posts Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant, with twenty guards bearing ceremonial swords; he firmly declined the directorship.

sentences.zh: 三年，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 服闋，改授中書監，侍中、護軍如故，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was reassigned as Director of the Secretariat, retaining Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, and was given one set of ceremonial drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was reassigned Director of the Secretariat, keeping Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, and was given ceremonial drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 時淮北屬，江南無復鰒魚，或有間關得至者，一枚直數千錢。

translations.literal: At the time the north of the Huai had fallen; south of the river abalone was no longer to be had, and any that reached the south by perilous routes cost several thousand cash apiece.
translations.idiomatic: The north bank of the Huai had fallen; abalone no longer reached the south, and any that did, brought by perilous routes, cost thousands of cash apiece.

sentences.zh: 人有餉彥回鰒魚三十枚，彥回時雖貴，而貧薄過甚，門生有獻計賣之，雲可得十萬錢。

translations.literal: Someone sent Yanhui thirty abalone; though he was already high in rank, he was desperately poor, and a student suggested selling them, saying ten thousand cash could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Someone sent Yanhui thirty abalone. Though already high in rank, he was desperately poor; a student suggested selling them for ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 彥回變色曰：「我謂此是食物，非曰財貨，且不知堪賣錢，聊爾受之。

translations.literal: Yanhui changed color and said, "I took this as food, not as goods for sale, and did not even know it could be sold for money—I accepted it only for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui flushed and said, "I took this as food, not merchandise, and did not even know it could be sold—I accepted it only for the moment.

sentences.zh: 雖復儉乏，寧可賣餉取錢也。

translations.literal: However poor I may be, how could I sell a gift for cash?
translations.idiomatic: However poor I am, how could I sell a gift for cash?

sentences.zh: 」悉與親遊噉之，少日便盡。

translations.literal: " He shared them all with friends and kin and ate them up in a few days.
translations.idiomatic: " He shared them with friends and kin and ate them up in a few days.

sentences.zh: 明年，嫡母吳郡公主薨，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: The next year his stepmother, Princess of Wu Commandery, died, and he wasted away to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his stepmother, Princess of Wu Commandery, died, and he wasted away to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，詔攝職，固辭，又以期祭禮及，表解職，並不許。

translations.literal: After the burial an edict ordered him to resume office; he firmly declined, and when the term for sacrificial rites arrived he submitted a memorial resigning—all were denied.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial an edict ordered him back to office; he firmly declined, and when sacrificial rites came due he submitted resignation—both were denied.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧暴虐稍甚，齊高帝與彥回及袁粲言世事，粲曰：「主上幼年，微過易改，伊、霍之事，非季世所行，縱使功成，亦終無全地。

translations.literal: As Emperor Cangwu grew ever more cruel, the future Emperor Gao of Qi discussed affairs with Yanhui and Yuan Can; Can said, "The ruler is still young; small faults can still be corrected. Acts like those of Yi Yin and Huo Guang are not for a decadent age—even if successful, there would be no safe ground in the end.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Cangwu grew ever crueler, Gao discussed affairs with Yanhui and Yuan Can. Can said, "The ruler is still young; small faults can be corrected. Yi Yin and Huo Guang's path is not for a decadent age—even success would leave no safe ground.

sentences.zh: 」彥回默然，歸心高帝。

translations.literal: " Yanhui was silent and gave his heart to Gao.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui was silent and gave his heart to Gao.

sentences.zh: 及廢蒼梧，群公集議，袁粲、劉彥節既不受任，彥回曰：「非蕭公無以了此。

translations.literal: When Cangwu was deposed, the assembled lords deliberated; Yuan Can and Liu Yanjie both refused appointment; Yanhui said, "Without Lord Xiao this cannot be settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangwu was deposed the assembled lords deliberated. Yuan Can and Liu Yanjie both refused office; Yanhui said, "Without Lord Xiao this cannot be settled.

sentences.zh: 」手取事授高帝。

translations.literal: " He took the business in hand and handed it to Gao.
translations.idiomatic: " He took the business in hand and handed it to Gao.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「相與不肯，我安得辭。

translations.literal: Gao said, "Since you all refuse, how can I decline?
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "Since you all refuse, how can I decline?

sentences.zh: 」事乃定。

translations.literal: " The matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 順帝立，改號衛將軍、開府儀同三司，侍中如故，甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Yanhui's title was changed to General Who Guards the Army, Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Dukes, retaining Palace Attendant, with fifty armed guards entering the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Yanhui became General Who Guards the Army and Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Dukes, keeping Palace Attendant, with fifty armed guards entering the hall.

sentences.zh: 及袁粲懷貳，曰：「褚公眼睛多白，所謂白虹貫日，亡宋者終此人也。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can grew disloyal in heart, he said, "Master Chu's eyes show much white—the so-called white rainbow piercing the sun; the man who will destroy Song is ultimately this one.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can grew disloyal at heart, he said, "Master Chu's eyes show much white—the white rainbow piercing the sun; the man who will destroy Song is ultimately this one.

sentences.zh: 」他日，粲謂彥回曰：「國家所倚，唯公與劉丹陽及粲耳，願各自勉，無使竹帛所笑。

translations.literal: " On another day Can said to Yanhui, "On whom the state relies are you, Liu of Danyang, and Can alone; I hope each will exert himself and not become a laughingstock in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: " Another day Can told Yanhui, "The state relies on you, Liu of Danyang, and me alone; let each exert himself and not become a laughingstock in the histories.

sentences.zh: 」彥回曰：「願以鄙心寄公之腹則可矣。

translations.literal: " Yanhui said, "I would gladly lodge my humble heart in your belly—that would be enough.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui said, "I would gladly lodge my humble heart in your belly—that would be enough.

sentences.zh: 」然竟不能貞固。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end he could not remain steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet in the end he could not remain steadfast.

sentences.zh: 及高帝輔政，王儉議加黃鉞，任遐曰：「此大事，應報褚公。

translations.literal: When Gao became regent, Wang Jian proposed adding the yellow battle-axe; Ren Xia said, "This is a great matter and should be reported to Master Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao became regent, Wang Jian proposed adding the yellow battle-axe. Ren Xia said, "This is a great matter and should be reported to Master Chu.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「褚脫不與，卿將何計？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "If Chu refuses, what plan will you have?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao said, "If Chu refuses, what plan will you have?

sentences.zh: 」遐曰：「彥回保妻子，愛性命，非有奇才異節，遐能制之。

translations.literal: " Xia said, "Yanhui protects wife and children and cherishes his life; he has no extraordinary talent or integrity—I can control him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia said, "Yanhui protects wife and children and cherishes his life; he has no extraordinary talent or integrity—I can control him.

sentences.zh: 」果無違異。

translations.literal: " In fact there was no opposition.
translations.idiomatic: " In fact there was no opposition.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之事起，高帝召彥回謀議，彥回曰：「西夏釁難，事必無成，公當先備其內耳。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Gao summoned Yanhui to counsel; Yanhui said, "The trouble in the western Xia will certainly fail; you should first secure the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Gao summoned Yanhui for counsel. Yanhui said, "The western rebellion will certainly fail; secure the interior first.

sentences.zh: 」高帝密為其備。

translations.literal: " Gao secretly made preparations accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao secretly made preparations accordingly.

sentences.zh: 事平，進中書監、司空。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Yanhui was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Yanhui was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏軍動，高帝欲發王公以下無官者從軍，彥回諫以為無益實用，空致擾動，上乃止。

translations.literal: When Wei armies moved, Gao wished to mobilize princes, dukes, and all below who held no office; Yanhui remonstrated that this would be of no practical use and would only stir disturbance, and the emperor desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei armies moved, Gao wished to mobilize princes, dukes, and every man without office; Yanhui remonstrated that this would serve no practical purpose and would only stir panic, and Gao desisted.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，帝親嘗酎，盛暑欲夜出，彥回與左僕射王儉諫，以為「自漢宣帝以來，不夜入廟，所以誡非常。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year the emperor was to taste the sacrificial brew in person; in the height of summer he wished to go out at night; Yanhui and Left Vice Director Wang Jian remonstrated, saying, "Since Emperor Xuan of Han, no one has entered the temple at night—this is to warn against the irregular.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year the emperor was to taste the sacrificial brew in person; in midsummer he wished to go out at night. Yanhui and Left Vice Director Wang Jian remonstrated: "Since Emperor Xuan of Han, no ruler has entered the temple at night—this warns against the irregular.

sentences.zh: 人君之重，所宜克慎」。

translations.literal: The weight of a ruler's person demands utmost caution."
translations.idiomatic: The weight of a ruler's person demands utmost caution."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷機事，彥回多與議謀，每見從納，禮遇甚重。

translations.literal: At the time Yanhui took part in many state deliberations; his advice was usually accepted and he was treated with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yanhui joined many state deliberations; his advice was usually accepted and he was treated with great honor.

sentences.zh: 上大宴集，酒後謂朝臣曰：「卿等並宋時公卿，亦當不言我應得天子。

translations.literal: At a great banquet the emperor, after drinking, said to the court, "You were all Song-era ministers and nobles—you cannot say I did not deserve to become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At a great banquet the emperor, after drinking, told the court, "You were all Song-era ministers and nobles—you cannot say I did not deserve to become Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」王儉等未及答，彥回斂板曰：「陛下不得言臣不早識龍顏。

translations.literal: " Before Wang Jian and the others could answer, Yanhui folded his tablet and said, "Your Majesty cannot say your subject failed to recognize the dragon countenance early.
translations.idiomatic: " Before Wang Jian and the others could answer, Yanhui folded his tablet and said, "Your Majesty cannot say your subject failed to recognize the dragon countenance early.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「吾有愧文叔，知公為朱佑久矣。」

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said, "I am ashamed before Emperor Guangwu—I have known you were my Zhu You for long."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed. "I am ashamed before Emperor Guangwu—I have known you were my Zhu You for long."

sentences.zh: 彥回善彈琵琶，齊武帝在東宮宴集，賜以金鏤柄銀柱琵琶。

translations.literal: Yanhui was skilled at playing the pipa; when Emperor Wu of Qi held banquets in the Eastern Palace, he was given a pipa with a gold-inlaid handle and silver pegs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was skilled at the pipa; when Emperor Wu of Qi held banquets in the Eastern Palace, he was given a pipa with a gold-inlaid handle and silver pegs.

sentences.zh: 性和雅，有器度，不妄舉動。

translations.literal: His nature was refined and elegant, with true capacity, and he did not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was refined and measured; he did not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 宅嘗失火，煙爓甚逼，左右驚擾，彥回神色怡然，索輿徐去。

translations.literal: Once his house caught fire and smoke and flames pressed close; his attendants panicked, but Yanhui looked calm, called for a carriage, and departed at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Once his house caught fire and smoke and flames pressed close; attendants panicked, but Yanhui looked calm, called for a carriage, and departed at leisure.

sentences.zh: 然世頗以名節譏之，于時百姓語曰：「可憐石頭城，甯為袁粲死，不作彥回生。」

translations.literal: Yet the age widely mocked his reputation for integrity; at the time the people said, "Pity Stone City—better die like Yuan Can than live like Yanhui."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age widely mocked his reputation for integrity; people said, "Pity Stone City—better die like Yuan Can than live like Yanhui."

sentences.zh: 高帝崩，遺詔以為錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Gao died, his final edict made Yanhui Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, his final edict made Yanhui Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，無單拜錄者，有司疑立優策。

translations.literal: Since the establishment of the Eastern Jin, no one had received a separate investiture as Supervisor; the relevant offices doubted whether a commendatory edict should be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Eastern Jin no one had received a separate investiture as Supervisor; the relevant offices doubted whether a commendatory edict should be issued.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉議，以為「見居本官，別拜錄，應有策書，而舊事不載。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian argued that "while holding the original post, a separate investiture as Supervisor should have an edict of appointment, but precedent does not record this.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Jian argued that "while holding the original post, a separate investiture as Supervisor should have an appointment edict, but precedent does not record this.

sentences.zh: 中朝以來，三公王侯，則優策並設；

translations.literal: Since the central dynasties, for the Three Dukes and princes both commendatory edicts and appointment edicts were issued;
translations.idiomatic: Since the central dynasties, Three Dukes and princes received both commendatory edicts and appointment edicts;

sentences.zh: 官品第二，策而不優。

translations.literal: for the second rank of office, appointment edicts but no commendatory edicts.
translations.idiomatic: for the second rank, appointment edicts but no commendatory edicts.

sentences.zh: 優者褒美，策者兼明委寄。

translations.literal: Commendatory edicts praise merit; appointment edicts also clarify the charge entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Commendatory edicts praise merit; appointment edicts clarify the charge entrusted.

sentences.zh: 尚書職居天官，政化之本，故尚書令品雖第三，拜必有策。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing stand at the head of heaven's offices and are the root of government and transformation; therefore though the Director's rank is third, investiture always requires an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing stand at the head of heaven's offices and are the root of government; therefore though the Director's rank is third, investiture always requires an edict.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書品秩不見，而總任彌重，前代多與本官同拜，故不別有策。

translations.literal: The Supervisor's rank is not specified, yet the overall charge is heavier; in former ages many were invested together with the original post, so no separate edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisor's rank is unspecified, yet the overall charge is heavier; in former ages many were invested together with the original post, so no separate edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 即事緣情，不容均之凡僚，宜有策書，用申隆寄。

translations.literal: Given the circumstances, he cannot be treated like ordinary officials; there should be an appointment edict to express the lofty charge.
translations.idiomatic: Given the circumstances, he cannot be treated like ordinary officials; there should be an appointment edict to express the lofty charge.

sentences.zh: 既異王侯，不假優文」。

translations.literal: Since he differs from princes and dukes, no commendatory text is needed."
translations.idiomatic: Since he differs from princes and dukes, no commendatory text is needed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋增彥回班劍三十人，五日一朝。

translations.literal: Soon Yanhui's guard of ceremonial swords was increased to thirty men, and he attended court once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yanhui's guard of ceremonial swords was increased to thirty, and he attended court once every five days.

sentences.zh: 頃之寢疾。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 彥回少時嘗篤病，夢人以卜蓍一具與之，遂差其一，至是年四十八矣，歲初便寢疾。

translations.literal: Yanhui had once been gravely ill in youth; a man in a dream gave him a set of divining stalks with one stalk missing, and he recovered; now he was forty-eight, and at the year's start he took to his bed.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yanhui had been gravely ill; a man in a dream gave him a set of divining stalks with one stalk missing, and he recovered. Now he was forty-eight, and at the year's start he took to his bed.

sentences.zh: 而太白熒惑相系犯上將，彥回慮不起，表遜位。

translations.literal: White Venus and Mars linked in succession and struck the constellation of the chief general; Yanhui feared he would not rise and submitted a memorial yielding office.
translations.idiomatic: White Venus and Mars linked in succession and struck the constellation of the chief general; Yanhui feared he would not rise and submitted a memorial yielding office.

sentences.zh: 武帝不許，乃改授司空、驃騎將軍，侍中、錄尚書事如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu did not permit this and instead reassigned him Minister of Works, General of Agile Cavalry, retaining Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu refused and instead reassigned him Minister of Works and General of Agile Cavalry, keeping Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 薨年四十八，家無餘財，負責數十萬，詔給東園秘器。

translations.literal: He died at forty-eight; the household had no surplus wealth and owed several hundred thousand in debt; an edict granted eastern-garden funeral vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight; the household had no surplus wealth and owed several hundred thousand in debt; an edict granted eastern-garden funeral vessels.

sentences.zh: 時司空掾屬以彥回未拜，疑應為吏敬以不？

translations.literal: At the time staff officers of the Ministry of Works, because Yanhui had not yet formally accepted the new post, doubted whether they should show the courtesy due a superior.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers of the Ministry of Works, because Yanhui had not yet formally accepted the new post, doubted whether they should show the courtesy due a superior.

sentences.zh: 王儉議：「依禮，婦在塗，聞夫家喪，改服而入。

translations.literal: Wang Jian argued: "According to ritual, if a wife is on the road and hears of mourning in her husband's house, she changes garb before entering.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian argued: "By ritual, if a wife is on the road and hears of mourning in her husband's house, she changes garb before entering.

sentences.zh: 今掾屬雖未服勤，而吏節稟於天朝，宜申禮敬。

translations.literal: Though the staff officers have not yet served in person, their official status comes from the court and they should observe ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Though the staff officers have not yet served in person, their official status comes from the court and they should observe ritual respect.

sentences.zh: 」司徒府史又以彥回既解職，而未恭後授，府應上服以不？

translations.literal: " Staff officers of the Ministry of Education also asked whether, since Yanhui had resigned office but had not yet formally accepted the later appointment, the ministry should observe mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: " Staff officers of the Ministry of Education also asked whether, since Yanhui had resigned but not yet formally accepted the later appointment, the ministry should observe mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 儉又議：「依中朝士孫德祖從樂陵遷為陳留，未入境，卒，樂陵郡吏依見君之禮，陳留迎吏依'聚女有吉日，齎衰吊'。

translations.literal: Jian argued again: "According to the Jin-era case of Sun Dezu, transferred from Leiling to Chenliu, who died before entering the new territory—the Leiling clerks observed the rites due a living lord, and the Chenliu welcoming clerks followed the rule 'when the bride has an auspicious day, carry mourning garb to condole.'
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued again: "By the Jin case of Sun Dezu, transferred from Leiling to Chenliu, who died before entering the new territory—Leiling clerks observed rites due a living lord, and Chenliu welcoming clerks followed the rule 'when the bride has an auspicious day, carry mourning garb to condole."

sentences.zh: 司徒府宜依居官制服。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Education should observe mourning garb according to office held.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Education should observe mourning garb according to office held.

sentences.zh: 」又詔贈太宰，侍中、錄尚書、公如故，增班劍為六十人，葬送禮悉依宋太保王弘故事，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: " An edict also posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, retaining Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and his ducal title, increased his guard of ceremonial swords to sixty, made burial and send-off rites follow the precedent of Song Grand Guardian Wang Hong, and gave the posthumous title Wen Jian.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, retaining Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and his ducal title; increased his guard of ceremonial swords to sixty; made burial and send-off follow the precedent of Song Grand Guardian Wang Hong; and gave the posthumous title Wen Jian.

sentences.zh: 先是庶姓三公，車需車未有定格，王儉議官品第一，皆加幢絡，自彥回始也。

translations.literal: Previously, for common-clan Three Dukes, the ceremonial canopy on the carriage had no fixed standard; Wang Jian argued that for the first rank of office all should add canopy tassels—this began with Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, for common-clan Three Dukes the ceremonial canopy on the carriage had no fixed standard; Wang Jian argued that first-rank officials should all add canopy tassels—this began with Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 又詔彥回妻宋故巴西主埏隧暫啟，宜贈南康郡公夫人。

translations.literal: An edict also granted Yanhui's wife, the former Princess of Brazil of Song, temporary opening of her tomb and the posthumously granted title Lady of the Duke of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also granted Yanhui's wife, the former Princess of Brazil of Song, temporary opening of her tomb and the posthumous title Lady of the Duke of Nankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 長子賁字蔚先，少耿介。

translations.literal: The eldest son Ben, styled Weixian, was upright and unyielding from youth.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Ben, styled Weixian, was upright and unyielding from youth.

sentences.zh: 父背袁粲等附高帝，賁深執不同，終身愧恨之，有棲退之志。

translations.literal: When his father turned against Yuan Can and the others to follow Gao, Ben deeply disagreed, bore lifelong shame and resentment, and wished to withdraw from the world.
translations.idiomatic: When his father turned against Yuan Can and the others to follow Gao, Ben deeply disagreed, bore lifelong shame and resentment, and wished to withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 位侍中。

translations.literal: He held the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彥回薨，服闋，見武帝，賁流涕不自勝。

translations.literal: When Yanhui died and mourning ended, Ben appeared before Emperor Wu and wept beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhui died and mourning ended, Ben appeared before Emperor Wu and wept beyond control.

sentences.zh: 上甚嘉之，以為侍中、領步兵校尉、左戶尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this and made him Palace Attendant, Colonel Director of the Foot Soldiers, and Director of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly praised this and made him Palace Attendant, Colonel Director of the Foot Soldiers, and Director of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 常謝病在外，上以此望之，遂諷令辭爵，讓與弟蓁，仍居墓下。

translations.literal: He often pleaded illness and stayed away; the emperor looked askance at this and eventually hinted that he should resign his title and yield it to his younger brother Zhen, remaining at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He often pleaded illness and stayed away; the emperor looked askance at this and eventually hinted that he should resign his title and yield it to his younger brother Zhen, remaining at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 及王儉薨，乃騎水牛出吊，以系門外柱，入哭盡哀而退，家人不知也。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian died, Ben rode an ox-cart out to condole, tied it to a pillar outside the gate, entered and wept with full grief before withdrawing; his family did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian died, Ben rode an ox-cart out to condole, tied it to a pillar outside the gate, entered and wept with full grief before withdrawing; his family did not know.

sentences.zh: 會疾篤，其子霽載以歸。

translations.literal: When he fell gravely ill, his son Ji had him carried home.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell gravely ill, his son Ji had him carried home.

sentences.zh: 疾小間，知非故處，大怒，不肯復飲食，內外合悉釘塞之，不與人相聞，數日裁餘氣息。

translations.literal: When the illness eased slightly and he saw he was not in his old place, he flew into a rage, refused food and drink, and had every door and window nailed shut so that no one could speak with him; after several days only a breath remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness eased slightly and he saw he was not in his old place, he flew into a rage, refused food and drink, and had every door and window nailed shut so no one could speak with him; after several days only a breath remained.

sentences.zh: 謝伷聞其弊，往候之，排合不可開，以杵捶破，進見賁曰：「事之不可得者身也，身之不可全者名也，名與身俱滅者君也，豈不全之哉！

translations.literal: Xie You heard of his distress and went to visit; he could not open the doors, smashed them with a pestle, entered, and said to Ben, "What cannot be obtained is the body; what the body cannot preserve is reputation; what destroys reputation together with the body is the ruler—how can reputation not be preserved!
translations.idiomatic: Xie You heard of his distress and went to visit; he could not open the doors, smashed them with a pestle, entered, and said to Ben, "What cannot be obtained is the body; what the body cannot preserve is reputation; what destroys reputation together with the body is the ruler—how can reputation not be preserved!

sentences.zh: 」賁曰：「吾少無人間心，豈身名之可慕。

translations.literal: " Ben said, "From youth I have had no worldly heart—how could body and reputation be worth coveting?
translations.idiomatic: " Ben said, "From youth I have had no worldly heart—how could body and reputation be worth coveting?

sentences.zh: 但願啟手歸全，必在舊隴。

translations.literal: I only wish, when death comes, to be laid out whole and buried in the old mound.
translations.idiomatic: I only wish, when death comes, to be laid out whole and buried in the old mound.

sentences.zh: 兒輩不才，未達餘趣，移屍徙殯，失吾素心，更以此為恨耳。

translations.literal: My sons are without talent and did not grasp my intent; moving the corpse and shifting the coffin betrayed my lifelong wish—that is my added grief.
translations.idiomatic: My sons are without talent and did not grasp my intent; moving the corpse and shifting the coffin betrayed my lifelong wish—that is my added grief.

sentences.zh: 」永明七年卒。

translations.literal: " He died in the seventh year of Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in Yongming 7.

sentences.zh: 蓁字茂緒，位義興太守。

translations.literal: Zhen, styled Maoxu, held the post of Grand Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, styled Maoxu, held the post of Grand Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 八年，改封巴東郡公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Badong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Badong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 明年，表讓封還賁子霽，詔許之。

translations.literal: The next year he submitted a memorial yielding the fief to Ben's son Ji; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he submitted a memorial yielding the fief to Ben's son Ji; an edict permitted this.

sentences.zh: 建武末，蓁位太子詹事、度支尚書，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Late in Jianwu, Zhen held the posts of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu, Zhen held the posts of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 永元元年卒，贈太常，諡穆子。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongyuan; posthumously granted Grand Minister of Ceremonies; posthumous title Mu Zi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongyuan 1; posthumously granted Grand Minister of Ceremonies; posthumous title Mu Zi.

sentences.zh: 蓁子向字景政，年數歲，父母相繼亡沒，哀毀若成人，親表異之。

translations.literal: Zhen's son Xiang, styled Jingzheng, was only a few years old when his parents died in succession; he mourned as if already adult, and relatives marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Xiang, styled Jingzheng, was only a few years old when his parents died in succession; he mourned as if already adult, and relatives marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 及長，淹雅有器量，位長兼侍中。

translations.literal: When grown, he was refined and possessed true capacity; he held the post of Regular Attendant with extended tenure.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he was refined and possessed true capacity; he held the post of Regular Attendant with extended tenure.

sentences.zh: 向風儀端麗，眉目如畫，每公庭就列，為眾所瞻望焉。

translations.literal: Xiang had elegant bearing and features like a painted portrait; whenever he took his place at public assembly, all looked up at him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had elegant bearing and features like a painted portrait; whenever he took his place at public assembly, all looked up at him.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，卒于北中郎廬陵王長史。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he died as chief secretary to the Prince of Luling, North Central Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Liang, he died as chief secretary to the Prince of Luling, North Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 子翔。

translations.literal: His son was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 翔字世舉，起家秘書郎，累遷宣城王主簿。

translations.literal: Xiang, styled Shiju, began his career as Secretary of the Secretariat and rose to chief secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, styled Shiju, began his career as Secretary of the Secretariat and rose to chief secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 中大通五年，梁武帝宴群臣樂游苑，別詔翔與王訓為二十韻詩，限三刻成。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Wu of Liang feasted the ministers at Leyou Garden and separately ordered Xiang and Wang Xun to compose twenty-rhyme poems within three quarters of an hour.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 5 Emperor Wu of Liang feasted the ministers at Leyou Garden and separately ordered Xiang and Wang Xun to compose twenty-rhyme poems within three quarters of an hour.

sentences.zh: 翔於坐立奏，帝異焉，即日補宣城王文學，俄遷友。

translations.literal: Xiang presented his while seated or standing; the emperor marveled, and that same day appointed him Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng, soon promoted to Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang presented his while seated or standing; the emperor marveled, and that same day appointed him Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng, soon promoted to Companion.

sentences.zh: 時宣城友、文學加正王二等，翔超為之，時論美焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Companion and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng ranked two grades below the prince proper; Xiang was promoted above this, and opinion of the time praised it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Companion and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng ranked two grades below the prince proper; Xiang was promoted above this, and opinion praised it.

sentences.zh: 出為義興太守，在政潔己，省繁苛，去游費，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Sent out as Grand Administrator of Yixing, he governed with clean self-restraint, reduced burdensome regulations, cut wasteful expenses, and the people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Grand Administrator of Yixing, he governed with clean self-restraint, reduced burdensome regulations, cut wasteful expenses, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 郡西亭有古樹，積年枯死，翔至郡，忽更生枝葉，咸以為善政所感。

translations.literal: In the western pavilion of the commandery was an ancient tree that had been dead for years; when Xiang arrived, it suddenly put forth branches and leaves again, and all took this as a response to good government.
translations.idiomatic: In the western pavilion of the commandery was an ancient tree dead for years; when Xiang arrived it suddenly put forth branches and leaves again, and all took this as a response to good government.

sentences.zh: 以秩滿，吏人詣闕請之，敕許焉。

translations.literal: When his term ended, officials and people went to the capital to petition for his retention; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, officials and people went to the capital to petition for his retention; an edict permitted this.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為吏部郎，去郡，百姓無老少追送出境，涕泣拜辭。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; on leaving the commandery, people young and old followed him to the border, weeping and bowing in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; on leaving the commandery, people young and old followed him to the border, weeping and bowing in farewell.

sentences.zh: 翔居小選公清，不為請屬易意，號為平允。

translations.literal: Xiang held the junior selection office with public integrity and did not change his mind for requests or connections; he was called even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang held the junior selection office with public integrity and did not change his mind for requests or connections; he was called even-handed.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，守吏部尚書，丁母憂，以毀卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he acted as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, entered mourning for his mother, and died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing 2 he acted as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, entered mourning for his mother, and died from grief.

sentences.zh: 翔少有孝行，為侍中時，母病篤，請沙門祈福，中夜忽見戶外有異光，又聞空中彈指。

translations.literal: Xiang had shown filial conduct from youth; when he was Palace Attendant his mother fell gravely ill, and he asked Buddhist monks to pray for blessing; in the middle of the night he suddenly saw strange light outside the door and heard fingers snapping in the air.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had shown filial conduct from youth; when he was Palace Attendant his mother fell gravely ill, and he asked Buddhist monks to pray; in the middle of the night he suddenly saw strange light outside the door and heard fingers snapping in the air.

sentences.zh: 及旦，疾遂愈，咸以為精誠所致云。

translations.literal: By dawn the illness was cured; all believed this came from sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the illness was cured; all believed this came from sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 建元中，為吳郡太守，百姓李道念以公事到郡，澄見謂曰：「汝有重疾。

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era he was Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery; the commoner Li Daonian came to the commandery on official business, and Cheng saw him and said, "You have a grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyuan era he was Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery; the commoner Li Daonian came on official business, and Cheng saw him and said, "You have a grave illness.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「舊有冷疾，至今五年，眾醫不差。

translations.literal: " He answered, "I have had a cold ailment for five years now; many physicians have failed to cure it.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I have had a cold ailment for five years; many physicians have failed to cure it.

sentences.zh: 」澄為診脈，謂曰：「汝病非冷非熱，當是食白瀹雞子過多所致。

translations.literal: " Cheng felt his pulse and said, "Your illness is neither cold nor hot—it must come from eating too many plain-boiled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng felt his pulse and said, "Your illness is neither cold nor hot—it must come from eating too many plain-boiled eggs.

sentences.zh: 」令取蘇一升煮服之。

translations.literal: " He ordered one sheng of perilla boiled and taken.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered one sheng of perilla boiled and taken.

sentences.zh: 始一服，乃吐出一物，如升，涎裹之動，開看是雞雛，羽翅爪距具足，能行走。

translations.literal: After the first dose he vomited up a thing about a sheng in size, wrapped in saliva and moving; when opened it was a chick with wings, claws, and spurs complete, able to walk.
translations.idiomatic: After the first dose he vomited up a thing about a sheng in size, wrapped in saliva and moving; when opened it was a chick with wings, claws, and spurs complete, able to walk.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「此未盡。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "This is not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "This is not yet finished.

sentences.zh: 」更服所餘藥，又吐得如向者雞十三頭，而病都差，當時稱妙。

translations.literal: " After taking the remaining medicine he vomited up thirteen more chicks like the first, and the illness was wholly cured; at the time this was called marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: " After taking the remaining medicine he vomited up thirteen more chicks like the first, and the illness was wholly cured; at the time this was called marvelous.

sentences.zh: 豫章王感病，高帝召澄為療，立愈。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yuzhang fell ill, Gao summoned Cheng to treat him and he recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yuzhang fell ill, Gao summoned Cheng to treat him and he recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左戶尚書。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Director of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Director of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 彥回薨，澄以錢一萬一千就招提寺贖高帝所賜彥回白貂坐褥，壞作裘及纓，又贖彥回介幘犀導及彥回常所乘黃牛。

translations.literal: When Yanhui died, Cheng used eleven thousand cash to redeem from Zhaoti Temple the white sable sitting rug Gao had given Yanhui, cut it up to make a fur coat and tassels, and also redeemed Yanhui's kerchief with horn pin and the yellow ox he usually rode.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhui died, Cheng used eleven thousand cash to redeem from Zhaoti Temple the white sable sitting rug Gao had given Yanhui, cut it up to make a fur coat and tassels, and also redeemed Yanhui's kerchief with horn pin and the yellow ox he usually rode.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，為御史中丞袁彖所奏，免官禁錮，見原。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was impeached by Imperial Censor Yuan Yan and dismissed, confined, then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 1 he was impeached by Imperial Censor Yuan Yan, dismissed, confined, then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，領右軍將軍，以勤謹見知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and General of the Right Army and was known for diligence and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and General of the Right Army and was known for diligence and prudence.

sentences.zh: 澄女為東昏皇后。

translations.literal: Cheng's daughter became empress to Emperor Donghun.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's daughter became empress to Emperor Donghun.

sentences.zh: 永元元年卒，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongyuan; posthumously granted Grand Master of the Purple-Gold Seal and Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongyuan 1; posthumously granted Grand Master of the Purple-Gold Seal and Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 照字彥宣，彥回從父弟也。

translations.literal: Zhao, styled Yansuan, was Yanhui's younger cousin on his father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, styled Yansuan, was Yanhui's younger cousin on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 父法顯，鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Faxian was Grand Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Faxian was Grand Administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 照少有高節，王儉嘗稱才堪保傅。

translations.literal: Zhao had lofty integrity from youth; Wang Jian once said his talent suited the posts of tutor and preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had lofty integrity from youth; Wang Jian once said his talent suited tutor and preceptor.

sentences.zh: 為安成郡還，以一目眇，召為國子博士，不拜。

translations.literal: Returning from An Cheng Commandery with one eye blinded, he was summoned as Doctor of the National University and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from An Cheng Commandery with one eye blinded, he was summoned as Doctor of the National University and refused.

sentences.zh: 常非彥回身事二代。

translations.literal: He often condemned Yanhui for serving two dynasties in one lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: He often condemned Yanhui for serving two dynasties in one lifetime.

sentences.zh: 彥回子賁往問訊照，照問曰：「司空今日何在？

translations.literal: Yanhui's son Ben went to inquire after Zhao; Zhao asked, "Where is the Minister of Works today?
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui's son Ben went to inquire after Zhao; Zhao asked, "Where is the Minister of Works today?

sentences.zh: 」賁曰：「奉璽紱，在齊大司馬門。

translations.literal: " Ben said, "Bearing the seal and cord, at the gate of the Grand Marshal of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " Ben said, "Bearing the seal and cord, at the gate of the Grand Marshal of Qi.

sentences.zh: 」照正色曰：「不知汝家司空將一家物與一家，亦復何謂。

translations.literal: " Zhao said with stern countenance, "I did not know your family's Minister of Works would hand one family's possessions to another family—what is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao said with stern countenance, "I did not know your family's Minister of Works would hand one family's possessions to another—what is there to say?

sentences.zh: 」彥回拜司徒，賓客滿坐，照歎曰：「彥回少立名行，何意披猖至此！

translations.literal: " When Yanhui received appointment as Minister of Education, guests filled the hall; Zhao sighed and said, "Yanhui established his name and conduct in youth—how did he come to this wild disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: " When Yanhui received appointment as Minister of Education, guests filled the hall; Zhao sighed, "Yanhui established his name and conduct in youth—how did he come to this wild disgrace!

sentences.zh: 門戶不幸，乃復有今日之拜。

translations.literal: The clan is unfortunate to have this appointment today.
translations.idiomatic: The clan is unfortunate to have this appointment today.

sentences.zh: 使彥回作中書郎而死，不當是一名士邪？

translations.literal: If Yanhui had died as a Secretariat Gentleman, would he not have been a true gentleman?
translations.idiomatic: If Yanhui had died as a Secretariat Gentleman, would he not have been a true gentleman?

sentences.zh: 名德不昌，遂有期頤之壽。」

translations.literal: Fame and virtue did not flourish, yet he lived to old age."
translations.idiomatic: Fame and virtue did not flourish, yet he lived to old age."

sentences.zh: 彥回性好戲，以軺車給之，照大怒曰：「著此辱門戶，那可令人見。
