translations.literal: Yanhui loved jesting and gave him a light carriage; Zhao flew into a rage and said, "Wearing this shames the clan—how can one let people see it?
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui loved jesting and gave him a light carriage; Zhao flew into a rage and said, "Wearing this shames the clan—how can one let people see it?

sentences.zh: 」索火燒之，馭人奔車乃免。

translations.literal: " He demanded fire and burned it; the driver fled with the carriage and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " He demanded fire and burned it; the driver fled with the carriage and escaped.

sentences.zh: 照弟炫。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Xuan.

sentences.zh: 炫字彥緒，少清簡，為從舅王景文所知。

translations.literal: Xuan, styled Yanxu, was pure and spare from youth and was appreciated by his maternal uncle Wang Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Yanxu, was pure and spare from youth and was appreciated by his maternal uncle Wang Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 從兄彥回謂人曰：「從弟廉勝獨立，乃十倍於我。」

translations.literal: His cousin Yanhui told others, "My cousin's integrity and independence surpass mine tenfold."
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yanhui told others, "My cousin's integrity and independence surpass mine tenfold."

sentences.zh: 為正員郎。

translations.literal: He served as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從宋明帝射雉，帝至日中無所得，甚猜羞，召問侍臣曰：「吾旦來如皋，遂空行可笑。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Ming of Song on a pheasant hunt, the emperor reached midday without taking anything and felt deeply ashamed and angry; he summoned the attending ministers and said, "I came out early to the marsh and returned empty-handed—laughable.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Ming of Song on a pheasant hunt, the emperor reached midday without taking anything and felt deeply ashamed; he summoned the attending ministers and said, "I came out early to the marsh and returned empty-handed—laughable.

sentences.zh: 」坐者莫答，炫獨曰：「今節候雖適，而雲霧尚凝，故斯翬之禽，驕心未警。

translations.literal: " Those seated did not answer; Xuan alone said, "Though the season is right, clouds and mist still linger, so these feathered birds remain proud and unalarmed.
translations.idiomatic: " Those seated did not answer; Xuan alone said, "Though the season is right, clouds and mist still linger, so these feathered birds remain proud and unalarmed.

sentences.zh: 但得神駕遊豫，群情便可載驩。

translations.literal: If only the divine carriage may roam in pleasure, the feelings of the crowd can still be filled with joy.
translations.idiomatic: If only the divine carriage may roam in pleasure, the feelings of the crowd can still be filled with joy.

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，乃於雉場置酒。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mood eased, and wine was set out at the pheasant field.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's mood eased, and wine was set out at the pheasant field.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎、司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Right Chief Secretary to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Right Chief Secretary to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 升明初，炫以清尚，與彭城劉俁、陳郡謝朏、濟陽江斅入殿侍文義，號為四友。

translations.literal: Early in Shengming, Xuan, for his pure integrity, entered the hall with Liu Hou of Pengcheng, Xie Tiao of Chen Commandery, and Jiang Jiao of Jiyang to attend on literary discussion and was called the Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shengming, Xuan, for his pure integrity, entered the hall with Liu Hou of Pengcheng, Xie Tiao of Chen Commandery, and Jiang Jiao of Jiyang to attend on literary discussion and was called the Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 齊台建，為侍中，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, he became Palace Attendant and Colonel Director of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established, he became Palace Attendant and Colonel Director of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 以家貧，建元初，出補東陽太守。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor, at the start of Jianyuan he went out to serve as Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was poor, at the start of Jianyuan he went out to serve as Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 前後三為侍中，與從兄彥回操行不同，故彥回之世，不至大官。

translations.literal: Three times he served as Palace Attendant; his conduct differed from his cousin Yanhui's, so during Yanhui's lifetime he never reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he served as Palace Attendant; his conduct differed from his cousin Yanhui's, so during Yanhui's lifetime he never reached high office.

sentences.zh: 澐字士洋。

translations.literal: Yun, styled Shiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, styled Shiyang.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為曲阿令。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he was magistrate of Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Liang, he was magistrate of Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 曆晉安王中錄事，正員郎，烏程令。

translations.literal: He rose through Recorder to the Prince of Jin'an, Regular Attendant, and magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Recorder to the Prince of Jin'an, Regular Attendant, and magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 兄游亡，棄縣還，為太尉屬，延陵令，中書侍郎，太子率更令，御史中丞，湘東王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When his elder brother You died, he abandoned his county post and returned; he served as aide to the Grand Commandant, magistrate of Yanling, Secretariat Gentleman, Director of the Heir Apparent's Music Office, Imperial Censor, and Staff Officer to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother You died, he abandoned his county post and returned; he served as aide to the Grand Commandant, magistrate of Yanling, Secretariat Gentleman, Director of the Heir Apparent's Music Office, Imperial Censor, and Staff Officer to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 澐之為縣令，清慎可紀。

translations.literal: As a county magistrate, Yun was clean and prudent enough to be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: As a county magistrate, Yun was clean and prudent enough to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 好學，解音律，重賓客，雅為湘東王所親愛。

translations.literal: He loved learning, understood music, honored guests, and was graciously beloved by the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, understood music, honored guests, and was graciously beloved by the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 澐子蒙位太子舍人。

translations.literal: Yun's son Meng held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son Meng held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蒙子玠。

translations.literal: Meng's son Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's son Jie.

sentences.zh: 玠字溫理，九歲而孤，為叔父驃騎從事中郎隨所養。

translations.literal: Jie, styled Wenli, was orphaned at nine and was raised by his uncle, Staff Officer to the General of Agile Cavalry Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, styled Wenli, was orphaned at nine and was raised by his uncle, Staff Officer to the General of Agile Cavalry Sui.

sentences.zh: 早有令譽，先達多以才器許之。

translations.literal: He had fine reputation early; elders mostly judged him talented and capable.
translations.idiomatic: He had fine reputation early; elders mostly judged him talented and capable.

sentences.zh: 及長，美風儀，善占對，博學能屬文，詞義典實，不尚淫靡。

translations.literal: When grown, he had handsome bearing, answered well, was broadly learned and able to compose prose; his language was classical and solid and did not favor decadence.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he had handsome bearing, answered well, was broadly learned and able to compose prose; his language was classical and solid and did not favor decadence.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，兼通直散騎常侍聘齊，還遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Chen he served concurrently as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication on an embassy to Qi; on return he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen's Tiancheng era he served concurrently as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication on an embassy to Qi; on return he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太建中，山陰縣多豪猾，前後令皆以贓汙免，宣帝謂中書舍人蔡景曆曰：「稽陰大邑，久無良宰，卿文士之內，試思其人。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era Shanyin County had many powerful scoundrels; successive magistrates were all dismissed for corruption; Emperor Xuan told Secretariat Attendant Cai Jingli, "Shanyin is a great district long without a good magistrate; among men of letters, try to think of someone.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era Shanyin County had many powerful scoundrels; successive magistrates were all dismissed for corruption. Emperor Xuan told Secretariat Attendant Cai Jingli, "Shanyin is a great district long without a good magistrate; among men of letters, think of someone.

sentences.zh: 」景曆進玠，帝曰：「甚善，卿言與朕意同。

translations.literal: " Jingli recommended Jie; the emperor said, "Excellent—your words match my thought.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingli recommended Jie; the emperor said, "Excellent—your words match my thought.

sentences.zh: 」乃除山陰令。

translations.literal: " Jie was then appointed magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: " Jie was then appointed magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 縣人張次的、王休達等與諸猾吏賄賂通姦，全丁大戶類多隱沒。

translations.literal: County men Zhang Cide and Wang Xiuda and various scoundrel clerks traded bribes and colluded in corruption; whole households of great families mostly concealed themselves from registration.
translations.idiomatic: County men Zhang Cide and Wang Xiuda and various scoundrel clerks traded bribes and colluded in corruption; whole households of great families mostly concealed themselves from registration.

sentences.zh: 玠鎖次的等，具狀啟台，宣帝手敕慰勞，並遣使助玠搜括，所出軍人八百餘戶。

translations.literal: Jie imprisoned Cide and the others, submitted a full report to the capital, and Emperor Xuan personally wrote to comfort him and also sent envoys to help Jie search and register; more than eight hundred military households were uncovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jie imprisoned Cide and the others, submitted a full report to the capital, and Emperor Xuan personally wrote to comfort him and sent envoys to help Jie search and register; more than eight hundred military households were uncovered.

sentences.zh: 時舍人曹義達為宣帝所寵，縣人陳信家富，諂事義達，信父顯文恃勢橫暴。

translations.literal: At the time Attendant Cao Yida was favored by Emperor Xuan; county man Chen Xin was wealthy and fawned on Yida; Xin's father Xianwen relied on influence and acted violently.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Attendant Cao Yida was favored by Emperor Xuan; county man Chen Xin was wealthy and fawned on Yida; Xin's father Xianwen relied on influence and acted violently.

sentences.zh: 玠乃遣使執顯文，鞭之一百，於是吏人股栗。

translations.literal: Jie then sent men to seize Xianwen and flog him one hundred strokes; thereafter clerks and people trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then sent men to seize Xianwen and flog him one hundred strokes; thereafter clerks and people trembled.

sentences.zh: 信後因義達譖玠，竟坐免官。

translations.literal: Later Xin slandered Jie through Yida, and Jie was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xin slandered Jie through Yida, and Jie was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 玠在任歲餘，守祿俸而已，去官之日，不堪自致，因留縣境種蔬菜以自給。

translations.literal: Jie held office for more than a year, living only on salary; on the day he left office he could not pay his own way home and stayed within the county border planting vegetables to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jie held office for more than a year, living only on salary; on the day he left office he could not pay his own way home and stayed within the county border planting vegetables to support himself.

sentences.zh: 或以玠非百里才，玠曰：「吾委輸課最，不後列城，除殘去暴，奸吏局蹐。

translations.literal: Some said Jie lacked the talent of a hundred-li magistrate; Jie said, "My tax deliveries and performance ratings were not behind other districts; I removed the violent and cleared out the cruel, and scoundrel clerks cowered.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Jie lacked the talent of a hundred-li magistrate; Jie said, "My tax deliveries and performance ratings were not behind other districts; I removed the violent and cleared out the cruel, and scoundrel clerks cowered.

sentences.zh: 若謂其不能自潤脂膏，則如來命，以為不達從政，吾未服也。

translations.literal: If you mean I could not enrich myself with grease and ointment, then as fate would have it—but to say I do not understand government, I am not convinced.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean I could not enrich myself with grease and ointment, then as fate would have it—but to say I do not understand government, I am not convinced.

sentences.zh: 」時人以為信然。

translations.literal: " People of the time believed this true.
translations.idiomatic: " People of the time believed this true.

sentences.zh: 皇太子知玠無還裝，手書賜粟米二百斛，於是還都。

translations.literal: The crown prince, learning Jie had no travel funds, personally wrote granting him two hundred hu of grain and millet, and he then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, learning Jie had no travel funds, personally wrote granting him two hundred hu of grain and millet, and he then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he rose to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 玠剛毅有膽決，善騎射。

translations.literal: Jie was firm, resolute, and bold in decision, and skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was firm, resolute, and bold in decision, and skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 嘗從司空侯安都於徐州出獵，遇猛獸，玠射之，載發皆中口入腹，俄而獸斃。

translations.literal: Once following Minister of Works Hou Andu on a hunt at Xuzhou, he met a fierce beast; Jie shot it, and every arrow struck the mouth and entered the belly; soon the beast fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: Once following Minister of Works Hou Andu on a hunt at Xuzhou, he met a fierce beast; Jie shot it, and every arrow struck the mouth and entered the belly; soon the beast fell dead.

sentences.zh: 及為御史中丞，甚有直繩之稱。

translations.literal: When he became Imperial Censor, he won great repute for straight measure.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Imperial Censor, he won great repute for straight measure.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，皇太子親制志銘，以表惟舊。

translations.literal: He died in office; the crown prince personally composed his epitaph to show regard for an old associate.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; the crown prince personally composed his epitaph to show regard for an old associate.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 所制章奏雜文二百餘篇，皆切事理，由是見重於世。

translations.literal: Memorials and miscellaneous writings he composed numbered more than two hundred pieces, all cutting to the heart of affairs; for this he was honored in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and miscellaneous writings he composed numbered more than two hundred pieces, all cutting to the heart of affairs; for this he was honored in the world.

sentences.zh: 子亮，位尚書殿中侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Liang held the post of Secretariat Attendant of the Palace Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang held the post of Secretariat Attendant of the Palace Hall.

sentences.zh: 論曰：褚氏自至江左，人焉不墜。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Since the Chu clan reached the Eastern Court, its men have not fallen away.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: Since the Chu clan reached the Eastern Court, its men have not fallen away.

sentences.zh: 彥回以此世資，時譽早集，及於逢迎興運，謗議沸騰，既以人望見推，亦以人望而責也。

translations.literal: Yanhui, with this hereditary standing, gathered early renown; when he met the rising fortune and courted it, slander boiled over—he was pushed forward by public esteem and also judged by public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui, with this hereditary standing, gathered early renown; when he met the rising fortune and courted it, slander boiled over—he was pushed forward by public esteem and also judged by it.

sentences.zh: 照貞勁之性，炫廉勝之風，求之古人，亦何以加此。

translations.literal: Zhao's upright, unyielding nature and Xuan's integrity surpassing others—sought among the ancients, how could one add to this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's upright, unyielding nature and Xuan's integrity surpassing others—sought among the ancients, how could one add to this?

sentences.zh: 玠公平諒直，文武兼資，可謂世業無隕者矣。

translations.literal: Jie was fair, honest, and straight, with both civil and martial gifts—one may say the clan's enterprise did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was fair, honest, and straight, with both civil and martial gifts—one may say the clan's enterprise did not decline.
